statement: Matrix multiplication is a binary operation producing a matrix product C = AB from two matrices A and B, defined when the number of columns in the first matrix A equals the number of rows in the second matrix B. If A has size m x n and B has size n x p, the resulting matrix product C has size m x p, with entries given by the sum of products of corresponding row and column entries: c_{ij} = \sum_{k} a_{ik} b_{kj}.

symbols.meaning: entry of the matrix product C at row i and column j
entry of matrix A at row i and column k
entry of matrix B at row k and column j

properties.why: Products may have different dimensions, one product may be undefined, or even for square matrices of the same size, products generally differ.

properties.property: Distributivity with respect to matrix addition: A(B + C) = AB + AC and (B + C)D = BD + CD.
properties.why: Results directly from coefficient distributivity via \sum_{k} a_{ik}(b_{kj} + c_{kj}) = \sum_{k} a_{ik}b_{kj} + \sum_{k} a_{ik}c_{kj}.

properties.property: Representation of function composition for linear maps: the matrix representing B \circ A is the matrix product BA.
properties.why: Applying the maps sequentially corresponds to associative matrix-vector multiplication (BA)x = B(Ax) = BAx.

properties.property: Representation of dot products: the dot product of two column vectors x and y is the unique entry of x^{\mathsf{T}}y.
properties.why: The resulting 1 x 1 matrix is identified with its single scalar entry.

assumptions.assumption: Inner dimensions match: the number of columns in the first matrix equals the number of rows in the second matrix.
assumptions.breaks_when: The column dimension of A does not equal the row dimension of B.

failure_modes.cause: The number of columns of matrix A differs from the number of rows of matrix B.
